reviewers.agent: claude general-purpose subagent, independent context, with the shortfall tree and a local agentops clone. Verified the pin's provenance against upstream (40-char SHA, v1.1.0^{commit}, on main, pyproject 1.1.0, range_patch_ids present), read enforce_platform_pin to confirm a pin mismatch really fails closed at exit 2, diffed v1.0.0..a900e56 for certification rungs, consumer-facing rules and gate severities, and reproduced the patch-id fallback's behaviour end to end on a fixture repo against both pinned versions.

the orchestrator independently re-derived the HIGH finding from source rather than accepting it: read attested_shas and check_range at a900e56, confirmed by_patch is populated from every shard in the tree with no ancestry filter, and grepped attest.py for merge-base/is_ancestor/--contains, finding none. Also caught and corrected its own error when a mis-scoped sed range made the secret patterns appear to have changed; a precise extraction showed them byte-identical.

records.finding: Bumping to v1.1.0 adopts a patch-id fallback that can be satisfied by an attestation from a different, already-merged PR, so a branch that was never reviewed passes the required gate at exit 0. attested_shas indexes every shard committed at head with no ancestry filter, and the pass condition is only set(ids) <= current. The sha join required a commit in THIS range to carry an attestation; the patch-id join drops that. A revert-then-reland reproduces a reviewed commit's patch-id inside a new range and inherits its shard — accidentally on an ordinary revert-and-reland PR, not only deliberately. Distinct from the documented git merge --squash limitation, which still required a review of the branch.
records.evidence: Reproduced on a fixture: old pin NO ATTESTATION exit 1; new pin PASS exit 0 with two uncovered commits. Source at a900e56: attest.py attested_shas populates by_patch from every shard filtered only on source=='attest'; check_range matches set(ids) <= current; no merge-base/is_ancestor/--contains anywhere in the file.
records.reason: Founder decision 2026-08-31, taken with the reproduction and the tradeoff in front of them: bump anyway and accept the window, because the rebase bug costs a full re-review on every PR that falls behind main (PRs #95-97 already paid it) while the exploit needs a revert-and-reland shape and the pass line names the uncovered commits. Filed upstream as workspace-dq6 with the mechanism, the reproduction and a suggested fix — refuse the fallback when the matched shard's attested sha is reachable from base, which leaves the rebase case this release exists to fix untouched. NOT fixed here: the logic is in agentops, and shortfall's shim is 24 lines.

records.finding: The rule stamps the platform version of the checker it documents — 'What the pinned mechanical checker (platform v1.0.0) actually fires on' — and the bump makes that disagree with repo.yaml's platform.pin. The version is written into the file precisely so a reader can tell which checker the list describes, and it is a protected path, so it cannot be corrected silently later.
records.evidence: repo.yaml now pins v1.1.0 and the shim reports warden 1.1.0, against the file's v1.0.0 stamp.
records.reason: Stamped v1.1.0. The list itself stays accurate: _SECRET_PATTERNS hashes identically at the v1.0.0 tag and a900e56, and no line was removed from mechanical.py across the bump — the only addition is a tests-accompany-logic checker, inert here since this file is shortfall's one engine:python rule.
